paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God isn't impressed by what we SAY, He cares about what we DO. The chief priests and elders asked Jesus where His authority came from, but they had already dodged the answer in front of them. When Jesus asked about John's baptism, they said, "We do not know," and I think that was less about not knowing and more about not wanting to say (Matthew 21:25-27). Friend, you can't hear the truth when you're busy protecting yourself.

Then Jesus tells the story of two sons, and it turns the whole thing around. The first said, "I will not," but later he changed his mind and went, and the second said, "I will, sir," and did not go (Matthew 21:29-30). Friend, the leaders themselves answer that the first son did the will of his father (Matthew 21:31). Then Jesus ties it to John: the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him, and the leaders did not (Matthew 21:32).

So here's what it means for you, baker: Jesus says the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before the leaders, because they believed John (Matthew 21:31-32). The leaders saw that happen and still did not repent and believe him (Matthew 21:32). A polite yes isn't enough, and a no can turn into belief when someone repents. And hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is not over.
